title: Choose the slate structure
question: Same colors, fonts and gray-signal rules; only the structure changes. The roll led with the command bar. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Command bar + plays digest
options.thesis: Jump anywhere by typing; the slate below is one dense row per game.
materials: one search field that filters rows live
dense game rows grouped by start window
options.viewport: Top bar: sport tabs and a wide 'Jump to a game, team or player' field. Below: a plays digest strip, then one row per game by kickoff window.
options.risk: Leans on typing; on a phone the rows lose columns and the command field is less natural.

options.label: Disagreement map + table
options.thesis: Every game and prop plotted model against market; the dots far off the line are the plays.
materials: model-vs-market scatter with a 'they agree' diagonal
sortable table linked to the dots
options.viewport: Left: a square map of model probability against market, gaps measured off the diagonal. Right: the same items as a sortable table; hovering one highlights the other.
options.risk: The map is new to visitors and needs one line of explanation; NFL and NBA dots stay gray, so only tennis picks pop.

options.label: Split view: list + game
options.thesis: Find the play and read the game on one screen: a compact list on the left opens the game inline on the right.
materials: side rail for sport and view
compact event list with plays pinned
options.viewport: Side rail (Tennis, NFL, NBA; Slate, Props, Model). Middle: plays pinned above a compact game list. Right: the selected game's market, model, movement, props and injuries.
options.risk: The most familiar shape (mail-client layout); on a phone it becomes list then full-screen game.
